scenes.name: No Limit Records y Master P
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Percy Miller, del Calliope Projects, más empresario que artista, abrió con los diez mil dólares de la indemnización por la muerte de su abuelo la tienda No Limit en Richmond (California), estudió el negocio, teloneó a Tupac y Too $hort y formó TRU con sus hermanos C-Murder y Silkk the Shocker. Priority le dio un contrato de distribución inédito: No Limit conservaba sus másteres y el 85 % de las ventas. Con su equipo de producción Beats by the Pound fichó a Mia X, Fiend, Mr. Serv-On o Kane & Abel y publicó a un ritmo frenético («Mr. Ice Cream Man», 1996): quince discos entre los cincuenta más vendidos, hasta su guardaespaldas rapeaba. De vuelta en Baton Rouge, lanzó películas (I’m Bout It), Mystikal y a Snoop tras Death Row; más de cincuenta discos y setenta y cinco millones de copias a finales de los noventa, y bancarrota en 2003. Soulja Slim fue asesinado justo antes de triunfar. «Hacemos música para el que tiene un altavoz en su Cutlass»: les enseñó a los raperos a ser empresarios.

podcast.title: Grammy Competition (1995)
podcast.body: Snoop Dogg was a dominant artist in 1995, the year Tony Bennett's low-charting "MTV Unplugged" album won Album of the Year. He represented the kind of contemporary music that the Recording Academy was criticized for overlooking in favor of more traditional acts. "In a year dominated by the likes of Green Day, TLC and Snoop Dogg".

podcast.title: Tupac Shakur Hologram Performance (2012)
podcast.body: Snoop Dogg performed at Coachella in 2012, featuring a groundbreaking appearance by a virtual Tupac Shakur on stage alongside him and Dr. Dre. Although billed as a hologram, the technology was a sophisticated version of Pepper's Ghost, creating a strikingly lifelike 3D image and marking a pivotal moment in the development of hologram performances. "Then in 2012, a very dead two-pock Shakur showed up at Coachella during a set featuring Dr. Dre and Snoop Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.title: 21st Century Videoclips - Problematic Content
podcast.body: Snoop Dogg's music videos from the 21st century are mentioned as containing content that can be considered even more "shameful" than many discourses found in Latin Trap. This point highlights that problematic lyrical and visual content is a broader issue across music genres, not solely inherent to Trap. "videoclips en pleno siglo veintiuno que son a veces incluso más vergonzosos que muchos discursos del trap latino."

xref.title: Extensive Live Performance History
xref.body: Biff Naked maintained an active touring career, performing alongside internationally recognized acts such as the Foo Fighters, The Smashing Pumpkins, Green Day, and Snoop Dogg. She also appeared in The Offspring's "The Kids Aren't Alright" music video, showcasing broad industry engagement. "she had a great live run too performing with everyone from the food fighters and the smashing pumpkins to Green Day and Snoop Dogg and if you know the offspring video the kids aren't all right she's in that one."

xref.title: Guest Stars and Hip Hop Royalty
xref.body: The show became known for its guest stars, and people tuned in weekly to see who would appear. It featured "hip hop royalty" such as Snoop Dogg, Christopher Kid Reed, Salt and Peppa, Biggie Smalls, and Outcast, reflecting Fox's strategy of leaning into the growing influence of hip hop. "The show actually became known for its guest stars, and people tuned in every week to see who else might show up."
